hyps.why: Adding a direct input-to-output edge where none exists helps far more than replacing an existing conv/pool edge.
Restoring the 0->3 edge from none gives a large gain compared with swapping an existing op.
With edge 3 removed, edge 4 is a main route to the output so a skip there helps much more.
Replacing none only re-adds an edge, giving a much smaller gain than upgrading an existing skip/pool edge.
Replacing a weak pooling edge with a 3x3 conv yields a large accuracy gain.
Pooling already provides some useful processing on edge 0, so upgrading to conv3x3 gains less than from none.
Going from a removed edge to a conv3x3 adds a whole new feature path, a larger gain than swapping ops.
Removing a learned conv3x3 edge hurts, whereas removing a skip or pool edge is nearly neutral.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing edge 0 cuts off the main path and hurts much more.
With edge 5 removed, the node-2 path cannot reach the output so upgrading edge 2 yields little.
